mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has risen monotonically from -16.3% to -11.6% over four weeks, signaling a sustained recovery trend. This upward momentum will persist over the next four weeks, driving RETAIL_REC further above baseline.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved 4.7 percentage points over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days does not exceed the mean of the last 28 days, or reverses to decline below -15%.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility has recovered from -28.9% to -16.4% over four weeks. When workplace attendance rises above -20%, commuters resume weekday retail visits and weekend shopping patterns, lifting RETAIL_REC within one week.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES at -16.4% in t-0w, above -20% threshold
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise in week t+1w despite WORKPLACES remaining above -20%, or WORKPLACES falls back below -20%.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT station usage has improved from -51.3% to -42.0% over four weeks, indicating restored commuting capacity. This enables retail foot traffic recovery; the relationship is direct and lagged by two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT improves by more than 5 percentage points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved 9.3 percentage points over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC in weeks t+2w and t+3w does not exceed the mean of the last four weeks, or TRANSIT reverses to decline below -45%.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility has been volatile (-9.0%, +5.4%, -21.0%, -7.1%) while RETAIL_REC declined steadily. When PARKS and RETAIL_REC move in opposite directions, it signals substitution of outdoor recreation for indoor retail. PARKS volatility will dampen RETAIL_REC recovery.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises above +5% while RETAIL_REC remains below -10%
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS at +5.4% in t-2w while RETAIL_REC at -16.0%
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above -8% over the next four weeks despite PARKS remaining elevated, or PARKS falls below -5%.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM has remained stable near +3% across all four weeks, indicating consistent essential shopping. This stability anchors consumer confidence and enables discretionary retail spending to recover alongside workplace return, with a four-week lag.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM remains above +2% for three consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days does not exceed the last 28-day mean, or GROCERY_PHARM falls below 0%.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility has declined from +9.6% to +5.9% over four weeks, indicating reduced stay-at-home compliance. When RESIDENTIAL falls below +7%, it signals policy relaxation or voluntary exit from restrictions, enabling retail reopening and foot traffic recovery within one week.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls below +7% for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL at +5.9% in t-0w, below +7% threshold
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise in week t+1w, or RESIDENTIAL rebounds above +8%.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT recovery from -51.3% to -42.0% combined with WORKPLACES recovery from -28.9% to -16.4% signals a coordinated return to pre-pandemic mobility patterns. This dual recovery drives RETAIL_REC upward over four weeks through restored commuting and shopping routines.
candidate_trigger: both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES improve by >5 percentage points over two weeks
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved 9.3pp, WORKPLACES improved 12.5pp over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days does not exceed the last 28-day mean, or either TRANSIT or WORKPLACES reverses by >8 percentage points.

mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC decline has slowed from -16.3% to -11.6% while TRANSIT remains severely depressed at -42.0%. This decoupling indicates retail recovery is driven by local foot traffic and delivery substitution rather than commuting. Recovery will stall if TRANSIT does not improve by >5 percentage points in the next week.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT fails to improve by >5 percentage points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved 4.7pp while TRANSIT improved only 9.3pp over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above -8% in week t+1w despite TRANSIT remaining below -40%, or TRANSIT improves by >5 percentage points.
